reference_drawer.title: 📖 Converse of BPT Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Rules and conditions for the Converse of Thales' Theorem.

items.rule: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then it is parallel to the third side.
items.example: Equal exact ratios establish the parallel condition.

items.rule: Calculate both side-division ratios independently before applying the converse.
When whole sides are involved, use the full-side ratio.
Set the two BPT ratios equal, cross-multiply, solve x, and verify positive segment lengths.
items.example: Do not swap the expressions attached to AD and DB.

items.rule: Corresponding leg divisions in a parallel-base configuration can be linked by proportionality.
items.example: Maintain the same top-to-bottom segment order.

concepts.title: 1. Converse of Basic Proportionality Theorem
concepts.subtitle: Equal side-division ratios imply parallelism
concepts.summary: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, that line is parallel to the third side.

points.text: Equal ratios imply parallelism by the converse.

schema_notes.strict_options_rule: Every strategy option and option_details text combines an instruction with actual mathematical content; every formula, ratio, or value in options is wrapped in single dollar signs.
schema_notes.diagram_rule: Every question contains an inline responsive SVG using the required 300×220 viewBox; checking diagrams have no parallel indicators while proof diagrams may show them.
schema_notes.latex_compliance: All equations, worked examples, and rubric mathematics use multiline aligned LaTeX with at most one equals sign per line.
schema_notes.guided_calculation_compliance: Every step has exactly two vertically stacked outputs and every field uses placeholder Enter value. Prompts and labels do not reveal answers.
schema_notes.pool_compliance: Each typology contains exactly 12 unique questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
